question:
In the given figure, BC parallel DE.

Find the value of x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/356cc5b8d7dbf60d37643478887adf7c4ea6bc418040fd3faa577ce2ddbce3af.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In geometry, when two lines are **parallel** (BC ∥ DE), the angles in identical relative positions at each intersection where a straight line (transversal) crosses them are equal.

These are called **corresponding angles**.

Since **BC ∥ DE**, the angle at B and the angle at D are corresponding angles.

∴ x = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **BC ∥ DE** in the provided figure.

**Property used:** When a transversal intersects two **parallel lines**, the **corresponding angles** are equal in measure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ccacf5ca888a420b68419f54ab88da4c3e591ca17a55e435056288b9e111e923.png] 

⇒ In the figure, triangle **ABC** is intersected by line segment **DE** such that **DE ∥ BC**.

⇒ Line **AB** acts as a **transversal** for the parallel lines **DE** and **BC**.

⇒ ∠ADE and ∠ABC are **corresponding angles** because they are on the same side of the transversal and in corresponding positions.

⇒ By the **Corresponding Angles Postulate**, ∠ADE = ∠ABC.

⇒ x = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the angles in the same relative position at each intersection are equal.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: AD/DB = AE/EC.

Similarity of Triangles

If DE ∥ BC, then triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC (ΔADE ∼ ΔABC) by the AA (Angle-Angle) similarity criterion.</p
